messages.bing: I am a US beginner with no coffee equipment. I want two milk-based espresso drinks each morning, made sequentially if needed, from whole beans. My hard budget is $800 for the complete equipment setup before tax and shipping, not per item. It must grind suitably for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk; integrated or separate equipment and manual or automatic milk preparation are all acceptable. Include necessary basic accessories or built-in equivalents, including a milk vessel where needed. Optional upgrades are not required. Prioritize enjoyable, consistent drinks, approachable workflow, reasonable maintenance, dependability, and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. Saving money matters; spending $800 is not a goal. Please return your strongest complete-setup options and useful machine or grinder alternatives that could combine with another provider's offers. Include a credible lower-cost alternative when available, and explain what any premium buys. Keep worthwhile alternatives available rather than showing only your top choice. Identify material seller, variant, or functionality uncertainties without treating routine specification omissions as disqualifying.
messages.google: I need a complete US-compatible espresso setup for a beginner who owns no equipment, making two milk-based drinks each morning from whole beans; sequential preparation is fine. The hard equipment budget is $800 total before tax and shipping. Grinding suitable for espresso, espresso brewing, milk steaming, and necessary basic accessories must all be covered. Integrated machines, separate machine and grinder combinations, and manual or automatic milk preparation are acceptable. I value drink consistency and enjoyment, easy daily workflow, manageable cleaning, dependability, and the actual seller's credibility and reasonable recourse. Please compare your strongest convenient integrated option and strongest separate-equipment option where available, keeping useful standalone components and credible less-expensive alternatives in your returned list. Components may be combined with another provider's offers. Explain meaningful benefits of paying more; the budget is a ceiling, not a spending target. Flag material variant or seller ambiguity, distinguishing the marketplace from its seller. Ordinary missing accessory or voltage details alone need not rule out a credible household offer.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Both receive the true total ceiling, essential capabilities, flexible configuration preferences, and satisfaction criteria. Different comparison emphases encourage breadth without excluding either configuration. No competitor offers or purchase commitments are asserted.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Both may favor offers near $800 or bundles that keep spending within their own catalogs. Explicit requests for cheaper alternatives and standalone components may broaden membership, although neither provider is obliged to cooperate. Separate emphases may reduce duplicated selections.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Budget disclosure risks price anchoring but helps prevent unaffordable or incomplete recommendations. Broad returned lists preserve the buyer's ability to compare seller risk, justify premiums, and combine components across providers.

messages.google: Please recommend good-value US-compatible home espresso equipment for a beginner starting from nothing and making two milk-based drinks each morning from whole beans. Sequential preparation is fine. Include integrated and separate-equipment alternatives where available, covering espresso-suitable grinding, brewing, milk steaming, and required basic accessories. Manual steaming and automatic milk systems are acceptable. Compare approachable workflow, consistent enjoyable drinks, maintenance, dependability, and actual seller confidence. candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Both receive functional needs and qualitative priorities; neither receives the numerical budget. Neither message invents a lower ceiling or promises a purchase.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Providers cannot anchor specifically to $800, but may interpret willingness to pay for improvements as scope for expensive offers. Requests for economical alternatives may help, without overcoming the incentive to maximize purchased revenue.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Could reveal attractive lower-priced options, but provides no reliable mechanism for doing so. Both lists could omit affordable complete setups, leaving fewer feasible choices at the final decision.

selection_reason: Plan 1 best protects feasibility and choice in a single-round game. Both providers can identify complete setups within the true budget, while requests for alternatives and complementary components support independent final comparison. Withholding the ceiling does not reliably induce lower prices or better selections from revenue-seeking recommenders.
limitations: No catalogs are visible, so forecasts concern incentives rather than particular products, prices, or sellers.
Providers control returned membership and order; requests for breadth cannot guarantee inclusion.
There is one round and no opportunity to recover omitted offers through follow-up. Final selection must assess the returned frozen offers against the full private brief.
